label.rationale: This is a YAML configuration template for the GraphRAG CLI's init command, not a prompt that asks an LLM to perform a task, so it has no LLM job to classify and no matching benchmark.

The prompt asks the model to assign a 0-10 float relevance/importance score to a given text under a domain and persona, which is a rating/judging job with no standard public benchmark dataset matching it directly.

The prompt asks the model to generate a role definition text by imitating a sample pattern for GraphRAG community reporting, which is a prompt-authoring/meta-generation job with no standard public benchmark.

The prompt asks the model to assign a short descriptive domain label to a sample text, which is topic classification, but the open-ended 'Domain:' completion with no fixed label set and no evaluation dataset means no standard benchmark applies.

The prompt asks the model to extract typed entities and relationships from a text into a fixed delimiter-based record format, which is structured information extraction (CoNLL-2003 named entity recognition uses entity-level F1 as its metric).

label.metric: entity-level F1 (exact match span and type)
label.rationale: The prompt asks the model to extract named entities of given types and relationships between them as a JSON list, which is structured information extraction (GraphRAG entity/relation extraction) rather than summarization or QA.

The prompt asks the model to extract entities with types and descriptions plus relationships with strengths from raw text into a fixed delimiter-based record format, which is structured information extraction (GraphRAG's knowledge-graph entity and relation extraction).

The prompt asks the model to read a text and emit a comma-separated list of entity type labels relevant to a task, which is schema induction for structured extraction rather than any standard public benchmark task.

The prompt asks the model to read a text and return a JSON array of entity type labels under an "entities" key, which is structured extraction, but no public benchmark dataset matches this schema-induction task closely enough to name one.

The prompt asks the model to pick the primary language of a text and reply with only the language name, which is a single-label classification whose output routes downstream prompt tuning; language identification benchmarks like FLORES-200 or Tatoeba exist but do not match this exact job closely.

The prompt asks the model to write a short expert persona description (a system-prompt-style role statement) for a given task, which is open-ended generation with no matching public benchmark or objective metric.

The prompt asks the model to condense a community's entities and relationships into a structured report with title, summary, rating, and grounded findings, which is a structured summarization job with no standard public benchmark matching it directly.

The prompt asks the model to merge a list of entity descriptions into one concise, coherent third-person summary, which is a multi-document summarization job with no standard public benchmark dataset matching this exact setup.

label.metric: entity-level micro F1 (exact span and type match)
label.rationale: The prompt asks the model to pull named entities of given types and their pairwise relationships out of raw text into a delimited, tuple-formatted list, which is information extraction rather than generation or QA.

The prompt asks the model to pull named entities and their relationships out of a document and return them as a JSON list, which is structured information extraction; CoNLL-2003 is the standard named entity recognition benchmark, scored by entity-level F1.

The prompt asks the model to pull named entities and relationships from a document into a delimited tuple format, which is an information extraction task whose closest public benchmark is named entity recognition scored by entity-level F1.

The prompt asks the model to write a structured community report (title, summary, rating, findings) from entity and relationship records, which is a generation-style summarization task with no standard public benchmark matching its grounded JSON report format.

The prompt asks the model to write a structured community report (title, summary, findings) from a set of entities, relationships, and claims, which is a generative summarization job with no standard public benchmark matching its exact format.

The prompt asks the model to pull named entities and structured claim tuples (subject, object, type, status, dates, source quotes) out of a document, emitted as delimited records with a completion token, which is information extraction rather than any of the other listed jobs.
The prompt extracts named entities (with types) and relationships from raw text into a delimiter-formatted list, which matches structured information extraction benchmarks scored by entity-level F1.

The prompt asks the model to merge multiple entity descriptions into one comprehensive, length-limited free-text summary, with no standard public benchmark matching this entity-description consolidation job.

label.metric: exact match / F1 on answer span (or human-graded answer faithfulness)
label.rationale: The prompt answers a user question using retrieved data tables as context, with inline citations to record ids and instructions not to fabricate, which is a retrieval-augmented generation answer task producing markdown free text.

The prompt has the model answer a question grounded in provided data tables with inline citations, while also emitting a self-assessed relevance score and follow-up queries as JSON, and no public benchmark dataset matches this combined grounded-answer-plus-self-scoring format.

The prompt synthesizes a markdown answer to a user query from retrieved GraphRAG community reports, with inline data citations and a general-knowledge fallback, which is a RAG answer-generation job without a standard public benchmark dataset mapping cleanly to it.

The prompt has the model answer a user query from retrieved community report summaries, returning a JSON with an intermediate answer, a relevance score, and follow-up queries, which is retrieval-augmented answering with extra self-scoring and query generation rather than a standard benchmark task.

This is the map step of GraphRAG global search: it asks the model to answer a user question from provided data report tables as scored, citation-backed key points in JSON, which is a retrieval-grounded answer generation job with no standard public benchmark dataset.

The prompt asks the model to merge multiple analyst reports into one markdown answer to a user question with citations and a word limit, which is multi-document synthesis in a RAG-style pipeline rather than a standard public benchmark task.

The prompt supplies retrieved data tables as context and asks the model to answer a user question in markdown with inline citations to those records, which is grounded retrieval-augmented answering rather than any standard benchmark task.

The prompt asks the model to generate a bulleted list of candidate follow-up questions grounded in provided data tables, which is question generation rather than any standard benchmarked task, so no clean public dataset analogue exists.

The prompt asks the model to rate relevance of a provided information passage to a question on a 0-5 scale with a JSON reason and rating, which is an LLM-as-judge relevance grading task rather than a standard public benchmark task (MS MARCO passage relevance judgments are the closest analogue, measured with nDCG@10 or MRR).
